stories.title: Trump gov't proposes more than US$103,000 fee on H-1B visas for skilled foreign workers
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump's administration has proposed a fee of more than US$103,000 on new H-1B visas for highly skilled foreign workers, a government notice on the Federal Register showed Monday. The Department of Homeland Security proposed a $103,265 fee for the H-1B visa program, designed for skilled professionals in the fields of science, technology, engineering and math, although a federal judge in June ruled that the fee was illegal. The department plans to receive public comments on the proposal for 30 days after the official publication of the Federal Register notice, which is set for Tuesday. "This fee would serve as a dedicated revenue mechanism to help recover a portion of the federal government's costs of administering the lawful immigration system," the department said in the notice. In September, Trump signed a proclamation to impose a yearly fee of $100,000 for an H-1B nonimmigrant visa application. The proclamation is set to expire next month as stipulated in it. The notice came as the Trump administration has been doubling down on its immigration controls under its America First policy. The H-1B program is subject to an annual worldwide cap of 85,000 visas.

stories.title: Some 25,000 people are seeking housing in Cali two weeks after Colombia's earthquake
stories.summary: The municipal survey in Cali, Colombia's third city with more than two million inhabitants, now covers 10,000 families affected by the magnitude 7.4 earthquake of August 10 and estimates around 25,000 people have been left without adequate housing. Many have spent recent days in shelters or with relatives while searching for a rental, in a market strained by the sudden loss of supply.

stories.title: 70,000 social and affordable homes to be built across England as part of £39bn plan
stories.summary: Ministers have announced where 70,000 social and affordable homes will be built in England over the next 10 years, in a bid to address the housing crisis. Funding has been granted to Greater Manchester, the West Midlands, West Yorkshire, South Yorkshire, North East England, and Liverpool, as well as £6bn for London. It is the first part of a wider plan to build 300,000 social and affordable homes across the nation, under the government's £39bn social housebuilding programme. Housing charities welcomed the news but said it was still not enough to meet demand, while the Conservatives said it was an "unfunded spending commitment". Of the new homes announced on Monday, 60% would be for social rent - which means the cost of the unit is about half that of market rents and there are strict criteria for who can apply for it. Prime Minister Andy Burnham said: "No child should be raised in a hostel room and no family should wait 10 years for a front door of their own. I have said from my first day in this job that everything starts with a good home." Under Labour, homeless figures have continued to rise to record levels. Data released earlier this month suggested 177,530 children were homeless in temporary accommodation. Natasha, who has been living in a hotel in Milton Keynes for the last four months with her son Zayd, is one of those waiting for a permanent home. The 22-year-old spent the final months of her pregnancy and the first weeks of her son's life living in a hotel. She says she has no idea how long she will be expected to stay there but was told it would only be temporary.

stories.title: UKMTO says it received report of tanker struck by 'unknown projectile' in Gulf of Oman
stories.summary: UKMTO says it received report of tanker struck by 'unknown projectile' in Gulf of Oman The UK Maritime Trade Operation said on Monday that it received a report from an oil tanker that it had been "struck by an unknown projectile" nine nautical miles northeast of Oman's Ash Shishah. The projectile reportedly caused damage to the engine room and disabled the vessel, with the environmental impact unknown, but all the crew are reported safe. stories.title: Lab-grown organoids are living longer — offering new insight into the human brain
stories.summary: A study in the journal Nature sets a new record for the lifespan of lab-grown cells called organoids. These clusters of human cells in petri dishes are used as models of the human brain.
